'''Mary Layne Boas''' (March 10, 1917 – February 17, 2010) was an American [[mathematician]] and [[physics]] professor<ref>[http://condor.depaul.edu/~physics/people/index.html DePaul Department of Physics] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100619130842/http://condor.depaul.edu/~physics/people/index.html |date=2010-06-19 }}</ref> best known as the author of ''[[Mathematical Methods in the Physical Sciences]]''<ref name=":0" /> (1966), an undergraduate textbook that was still widely used in college classrooms as of 1999.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Spector|first=Donald|title=Book Reviews|journal=[[American Journal of Physics]]|year=1999|volume=67|issue=2|pages=165–169|doi=10.1119/1.19216|bibcode=1999AmJPh..67..165R}}</ref>

==Education and career==
She received a bachelor's degree (1938) and a master's degree (1940) in mathematics at the [[University of Washington]], and a Ph.D. (1948) in physics at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name=obit/>
She taught physics at [[DePaul University]] in Chicago for thirty years, retiring in 1987 to return to Washington.<ref name=obit>{{Cite web|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/seattletimes/obituary.aspx?n=mary-elizabeth-layne-boas&pid=139866372|title=Mary Elizabeth Layne Boas's obituary in The Seattle Times|date=2010-02-20|website=The Seattle Times}}</ref> Prior to her time at DePaul University, she served as an instructor in the mathematics department at [[Duke University]].

==Contributions==
In 2005, at the age of 88, Boas published the third edition of her textbook.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|url=http://www.wiley.com/WileyCDA/WileyTitle/productCd-0471198269.html|title=Mathematical Methods in the Physical Sciences, 3rd Edition|last=Boas|first=Mary|date=2005-07-22|publisher=Wiley.com|language=en-us|isbn=978-0-471-19826-0|archive-date=2009-04-16|access-date=2010-06-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090416091309/http://www.wiley.com/WileyCDA/WileyTitle/productCd-0471198269.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> She established the Mary L. Boas Endowed Scholarship at the University of Washington in 2008 to recognize outstanding academic achievements by female students in physics.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.phys.washington.edu/awards.htm |title=Univ. Wash. Department of Physics awards |access-date=2010-06-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120428055447/http://www.phys.washington.edu/awards.htm |archive-date=2012-04-28 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Physics Award Recipients {{!}} Department of Physics {{!}} University of Washington |url=https://phys.washington.edu/physics-award-recipients |access-date=2026-04-20 |website=phys.washington.edu}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Mary Boas was married to mathematician [[Ralph P. Boas Jr.]] Her son, [[Harold P. Boas]], is also a noted mathematician. She died on February 17, 2010, at her home near [[Seattle, Washington]].
